title: Maps in a model localization from cofibrant to fibrant objects
statement: Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category as defined in [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test], with weak equivalences $W$, and let $\gamma:\mathcal M\to\mathcal H$ be an ordinary localization at $W$, in universes where it exists. Let $A$ be cofibrant and $B$ fibrant. Every morphism $\alpha:\gamma A\to\gamma B$ equals $\gamma(f)$ for some morphism $f:A\to B$. Moreover, for $f,g:A\to B$, $\gamma(f)=\gamma(g)$ if and only if there exist an object $J$, maps $e_0,e_1:A\to J$, a weak equivalence $c:J\to A$ with $ce_0=ce_1=1_A$, and a map $H:J\to B$ with $He_0=f$ and $He_1=g$. Such data are called a cylinder and a left homotopy; no cofibration condition on $(e_0,e_1):A\amalg A\to J$ is required in this assertion.
